## Goal
`ticks()` reads tagged ticks without a limit that matters (`checklist_state.py:27`) but finds the first dashboard version's untagged ticks (`broker_id` None) by looking at the newest 5000 events of every kind (`_LEGACY_SCAN`, `checklist_state.py:28`, read at `checklist_state.py:70`). The store cannot filter on a missing broker id (`storage/db.py:372-382`), and with a 400-site registry one scan writes about 400 events, so about 12 scans push an old tick out of the window and a checklist the person ticked long ago shows as not done again. Fix by migrating on read: when `ticks()` finds legacy ticks in the window, re-log each as a tagged tick (same `checklist`, original timestamp, action `DONE`/`UNDONE`) plus one marker event (`checklist_legacy_migrated`, detail `{"count": n}`), once; later reads look for the marker and skip the legacy scan entirely. The returned ticks are the same as today's for the same data.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Fake store with a legacy tick, then 6000 unrelated events: today's `ticks()` returns it only if migrated earlier; after the first call in a fresh store (tick inside the window) it is migrated and a second call after 6000 more events still returns it.
2. Migration is idempotent: a second call writes nothing; the marker event is present exactly once.
3. The migrated tick keeps its original timestamp, so ordering against newer tagged ticks is unchanged (newest wins).
4. A store with no legacy ticks writes no marker on read (reads stay writes-free when there is nothing to migrate) but still skips the legacy scan on later calls once the marker exists; with no marker and no legacy ticks the scan runs as before.
5. `ticks()` on a store whose `log` raises still returns the ticks (a failed migration never breaks a read; log a count only).
6. Existing checklist_state tests and WO-281 tests pass unchanged; `item_doc`, `list_doc`, `show_doc` output unchanged.
